props.html:
Open the mockup

Just look at itDouble click index.html. Every link in the navigation works and takes you to the next page in this folder.
Serve it insteadFrom this folder run python -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/. Identical result.
Check a page against the briefOpen research/page-design-fingerprints.csv. One row per page, with its section sequence.
Hand it to a developerSend them developer-handoff.html. It covers the production URLs, the shell, the schema and what to strip.

Why the links work locally

Every link in the markup carries the real production URL, for example /service/pressure-surface-cleaning/, because that is what gets imported. A small script at the end of each page rewrites those to the flat file names while you are reviewing, and turns itself off on a real domain. The delivered source is untouched. It is documented in the handoff under Preview bootstrap, and it is removed at import.

What is in the folder

File or folderWhat it is
index.htmlThe approved home page. Design locked, content unchanged from home-v7.html. The only edits are the image paths, which now use the production form.
the other .html pagesOne file per approved URL, named after the page. Flat, no folders.
site.cssThe one stylesheet, as a file. No page loads it: the same CSS is written into every page inside a single <style> block, so each page stands on its own. The file is here because the CMS wants this once, globally, rather than 148 copies.
site.jsThe one script, as a file, on the same terms: navigation, mega menu, quote drawer, form validation, scroll reveal, back to top, plus the preview bootstrap. No page loads it either — it is written into every page inside a single <script> block at the end of the body.
cms-implementation/The global header, the global footer and the two shared assets on their own, which is what goes into the CMS once rather than per page. global-header.html is the single source for the header, the navigation, the Quick Quote tab, the drawer, its form and its behaviour; every page in this folder carries exactly that block. Both components embed the logo, so neither depends on /uploads/ either.
uploads/Every image the pages reference. 24 supplied by the client, 35 generated for this build.
route-map.csvEvery production URL and the flat file that represents it.
research/The approved registers, the keyword and location research, the image asset register and the per page design fingerprints.
qa/Full page screenshots at five widths per page, and the scripts that produced the findings.

Two things to look at first

Resolved: the home page before and after section

The lede used to say that every pair was one of the client's own jobs, shot from the same spot. The four before files are named ...-before-SIMULATED-... and are generated, so the claim was not true. The section now presents the pairs as illustrative comparisons and points at Our work for photographs of real completed jobs. The layout, the images, the slider and the styling are unchanged.

The alt text on all eight images in that section was rewritten at the same time: the four after images no longer say “by Prime Exteriors”, and the four before images no longer describe themselves as the same property photographed earlier. A check in qa/claimqa.py now fails the build if a generated or unverified image is described as the client's own work.

No generated before and after pair is used on any internal page.

Some photographs are generated, and they are labelled

The client supplied 24 photographs, all square, which does not cover 148 pages. Where no genuine photograph fitted a page, an image was generated, as the brief authorises. Every one is recorded in research/image-asset-register.csv with its source, its subject and the prompt that produced it.

None of them is captioned or described as a Prime Exteriors job. Alt text describes what is in the picture and nothing about who did the work. Swapping any of them for a real photograph later is a file replacement, nothing more.

Six things the client can close

None of these stop the build. Each one makes a specific page stronger the day it is answered.

  1. Typical price ranges. The two cost guides carry no dollar figures, because there is no price list in the approved research and inventing a range would have broken the no-fabrication rule. They teach the pricing models instead, which is honest and useful. Real numbers would make them much stronger.
  2. Insurance certificate. This one needs an answer before launch. The home page states $20m public liability cover, in the before and after section. The verified business facts record no insurance certificate and list insurance under do not publish, so that figure is currently unsupported. Either supply the certificate, in which case the About page can carry it properly as well, or the figure should come off the home page. It has been left in place rather than removed unilaterally, because it is an approved trust signal and taking it out is a commercial decision, not a production one.
  3. Facebook and Instagram URLs. Both profiles are verified to exist and neither URL was captured, so neither is linked.
  4. An email address. Nothing on the site carries one, because none was verified. The contact page works without it and reads better with it.
  5. The business name against the ABN. "Prime Exteriors" is not registered against ABN 17 145 375 887; the registered name is Raqim Remedies. No ABN or business name trust signal is published anywhere until that is resolved.
  6. Work in Essendon, Preston, Bundoora or Dallas. If any of it exists, those council and suburb pages get stronger immediately. See the data correction note in the developer handoff.

Resolved: the thirteen headings that counted wrong

Thirteen headings stated a number that did not match what sat under them. All thirteen are corrected. Where the number earned its place it was made right; where it added nothing the heading reads naturally without one, which is usually better than “Seven things”.

windows-gutters-roof-solarThe four pages belowThe pages below. There are nine.

A sweep then checked every other heading and caption that states a number against the rows, cards, steps or links beneath it: 253 of them, and one more mismatch found, on concrete-resurfacing, which is in the table above. The check ships as qa/countqa.py and runs on every build. Headings whose number counts something the sentence names rather than the block beneath — “two systems” above eight rows comparing those two systems, for instance — were read individually and left alone.

What has been checked on every page

  • Rendered in headless Chromium over a local server, then measured. No check here is a reading of the source code.
  • Twenty four viewport widths from 320 to 2560, for horizontal overflow and for any element or line of text escaping its own container.
  • Colour contrast computed on flat backgrounds, and measured pixel by pixel where text sits on a gradient, a scrim or a photograph.
  • Target size against WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8, including the spacing exception rather than a flat 24 pixel rule.
  • Image density at every width, so nothing is displayed larger than its source.
  • Every internal link checked against the approved canonical register, and every resolved preview link checked against the files in the folder.
  • Console errors, failed requests, heading order, and any element marked hidden that still paints.
  • Page against page: sentence shingles, section headings and question sets, to catch two pages saying the same thing.
  • That every page carries the same global header as every other page, byte for byte, that it is cms-implementation/global-header.html, that the Quick Quote drawer exists exactly once per page and never inside page content, and that every quote control points at it and opens it.
  • Self containment: that no page loads a local stylesheet or script, that each carries exactly one style block and one script block, that no element carries a style attribute, and that every image is embedded rather than fetched.
  • The three step form driven end to end in a browser on six pages, through the panel and through the inline section, 186 assertions in all.
